AFP release images of children’s clothes found on electronic devices seized as part of investigation into Hamish Tait Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A tiny dinosaur puffer jacket could lead police to more victims of a former childcare worker and alleged prolific child sex offender. Federal police have released pictures of clothing from children they want to identify, urging parents and carers who recognise the items to come forward. Hamish Tait, 35, has been charged with 329 offences related to the creation and distribution of child abuse material alleged to have occurred at several of the 62 childcare centres he worked at or visited, primarily in Sydney. The clothes included the puffer jacket, shorts with a blue pattern, a T-shirt with an animal pattern and a two-tone T-shirt.

Welcome to the 7NEWS.com.au breaking news live blog. We’ll be delivering the latest on major crime, traffic and weather news throughout the morning and everything you might’ve missed last night. Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Detectives have called on the public for help identifying potential victims of a man accused of more than 300 child abuse offences. Australian Federal Police (AFP) on Thursday released seven images allegedly located on electronic devices seized during the investigation into​ former Sydney childcare worker Hamish Tait​. Police allege the 35-year-old’s offences occurred from 2009 to 2025 across 62 childcare centres Tait worked at, or attended, across Sydney. The identities of 136 alleged victims are known to police, with 22 yet to be identified.

Detectives found the images on electronic devices seized as part of their investigation into Tait. In about two days, officers have received more than 300 calls with information. “Every image may contain a clue that helps identify a child,” Australian federal police Det Acting Insp Emmanuel Tsardoulias said. “Our victim ID team is tenacious, they’re committed and will stop at nothing to identify children or victims of child sexual exploitation.” The detective admitted it was impossible not to consider the allegations and their potential impact as a parent himself. “We understand families want answers quickly, but we must be thorough to identify every victim to protect the investigation and ensure families receive the right support,” Tsardoulias said. Police believe the images were taken between 2018 and 2023 at childcare centres at Rouse Hill and Putney, in Sydney’s north-west.

AFP release images of children’s clothes found on electronic devices seized as part of investigation into Hamish Tait

A tiny dinosaur puffer jacket could lead police to more victims of a former childcare worker and alleged prolific child sex offender.

Federal police have released pictures of clothing from children they want to identify, urging parents and carers who recognise the items to come forward.

Hamish Tait, 35, has been charged with 329 offences related to the creation and distribution of child abuse material alleged to have occurred at several of the 62 childcare centres he worked at or visited, primarily in Sydney.

The clothes included the puffer jacket, shorts with a blue pattern, a T-shirt with an animal pattern and a two-tone T-shirt.

Detectives found the images on electronic devices seized as part of their investigation into Tait.

In about two days, officers have received more than 300 calls with information.

“Every image may contain a clue that helps identify a child,” Australian federal police Det Acting Insp Emmanuel Tsardoulias said.

“Our victim ID team is tenacious, they’re committed and will stop at nothing to identify children or victims of child sexual exploitation.”

The detective admitted it was impossible not to consider the allegations and their potential impact as a parent himself.

“We understand families want answers quickly, but we must be thorough to identify every victim to protect the investigation and ensure families receive the right support,” Tsardoulias said.

Police believe the images were taken between 2018 and 2023 at childcare centres at Rouse Hill and Putney, in Sydney’s north-west.

The investigation has identified a further six victims, reducing the total number of unidentified children to 16.

Tait has been in custody since being arrested and charged in July 2025, when police seized almost 2.5m files from electronic devices at his home.

He was initially charged with eight counts of online child abuse material offences, and was hit with additional charges through April, June and July 2026 which now total 329 charges.

It includes 162 counts of producing child abuse material and 81 counts of filming a person engaged in a private act without consent.

A non-publication order granted to the AFP to protect the integrity of the investigation was lifted on Monday after a legal stoush.

payload.title: Australian poliisi julkaisi kuvia lasten vaatteista mahdollisten uhrien tunnistamiseksi
payload.summary: Poliisi pyytää vanhempia ja huoltajia tunnistamaan Sydneyssä takavarikoiduilta laitteilta löytyneissä kuvissa näkyviä lasten vaatteita.
payload.content:
Australian liittovaltion poliisi AFP on julkaissut seitsemän kuvaa lasten vaatteista osana tutkintaa, jossa entistä sydneyläistä varhaiskasvatuksen työntekijää Hamish Taitia epäillään laajasta lapsiin kohdistuneesta rikoskokonaisuudesta. Takavarikoiduilta elektronisilta laitteilta löytyneiden kuvien toivotaan auttavan tunnistamaan lisää mahdollisia uhreja, ja poliisi pyytää vanhempia sekä huoltajia ilmoittamaan, jos vaatteet näyttävät tutuilta.

## Vaatteista etsitään uusia johtolankoja

Yksi poliisin erityisesti esiin nostamista vaatteista on pieni dinosauruksilla kuvioitu toppatakki. Muissa kuvissa näkyy sinikuvioiset shortsit, eläinkuvioinen T-paita ja kaksivärinen T-paita. Tutkijat löysivät kuvat elektronisilta laitteilta, jotka takavarikoitiin Taitia koskevan tutkinnan yhteydessä. Poliisin mukaan jokainen kuva voi sisältää yksityiskohdan, joka auttaa yhdistämään aineiston tiettyyn lapseen. Siksi myös yksittäisen vaatteen tunnistamista pidetään mahdollisena uutena johtolankana.

Poliisi arvioi, että kuvat on otettu vuosina 2018–2023 Rouse Hillin ja Putneyn alueiden päiväkodeissa Sydneyn luoteisosassa. Tutkijat ovat saaneet noin kahdessa päivässä yli 300 yhteydenottoa ihmisiltä, joilla saattaa olla tapaukseen liittyviä tietoja.

## Epäillyt teot ajoittuvat vuosille 2009–2025

35-vuotiasta Taitia vastaan on nostettu 329 syytettä, jotka liittyvät lasten seksuaalista hyväksikäyttöä kuvaavan materiaalin väitettyyn tuottamiseen ja levittämiseen. Poliisin mukaan epäillyt teot ajoittuvat vuosille 2009–2025. Tait työskenteli tai vieraili tuona aikana kaikkiaan 62 varhaiskasvatuksen toimipaikassa pääasiassa Sydneyssä, ja tekojen epäillään tapahtuneen useissa niistä.

Poliisi tuntee tällä hetkellä 136 epäillyn uhrin henkilöllisyyden, mutta 22 lasta on yhä tunnistamatta. Vaatteiden tunnistamisella voidaan siten saada uusia vihjeitä juuri niistä lapsista, joiden henkilöllisyyttä tutkijat eivät ole vielä pystyneet selvittämään.

Australian liittovaltion poliisin Emmanuel Tsardoulias sanoi, että jokaisessa kuvassa voi olla lapsen tunnistamiseen johtava vihje. Hän kuvasi uhrien tunnistamiseen keskittyvää ryhmää sitoutuneeksi ja määrätietoiseksi. Tsardoulias kertoi pohtivansa väitteiden mahdollista vaikutusta myös vanhempana. Hänen mukaansa poliisi ymmärtää perheiden halun saada vastauksia nopeasti, mutta tutkinta on tehtävä perusteellisesti, jotta jokainen uhri voidaan tunnistaa, rikostutkinta turvata ja perheille järjestää oikeanlaista tukea.
summary_bullets: Poliisi julkaisi seitsemän kuvaa takavarikoiduilta laitteilta löytyneistä lasten vaatteista.
Hamish Taitia vastaan on nostettu 329 syytettä, ja epäilty toiminta ajoittuu vuosille 2009–2025.
Poliisi tuntee 136 epäillyn uhrin henkilöllisyyden, mutta 22 lasta on edelleen tunnistamatta.
payload.journalist_note: Epäilyt ja syytteet on erotettu todetuista tosiasioista. Taitin kerrotaan työskennelleen tai vierailleen 62 toimipaikassa, mutta rikoksia ei väitetä tapahtuneen niissä kaikissa.

Poliisi tuntee 136 epäillyn uhrin henkilöllisyyden, mutta 22 lasta on edelleen tunnistamatta.

AFP release images of children’s clothes found on electronic devices seized as part of investigation into Hamish Tait Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A tiny dinosaur puffer jacket could lead police to more victims of a former childcare worker and alleged prolific child sex offender. Federal police have released pictures of clothing from children they want to identify, urging parents and carers who recognise the items to come forward. Hamish Tait, 35, has been charged with 329 offences related to the creation and distribution of child abuse material alleged to have occurred at several of the 62 childcare centres he worked at or visited, primarily in Sydney. The clothes included the puffer jacket, shorts with a blue pattern, a T-shirt with an animal pattern and a two-tone T-shirt.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Detectives have called on the public for help identifying potential victims of a man accused of more than 300 child abuse offences. Australian Federal Police (AFP) on Thursday released seven images allegedly located on electronic devices seized during the investigation into​ former Sydney childcare worker Hamish Tait​. Police allege the 35-year-old’s offences occurred from 2009 to 2025 across 62 childcare centres Tait worked at, or attended, across Sydney. The identities of 136 alleged victims are known to police, with 22 yet to be identified.

Detectives found the images on electronic devices seized as part of their investigation into Tait. In about two days, officers have received more than 300 calls with information. “Every image may contain a clue that helps identify a child,” Australian federal police Det Acting Insp Emmanuel Tsardoulias said. “Our victim ID team is tenacious, they’re committed and will stop at nothing to identify children or victims of child sexual exploitation.” The detective admitted it was impossible not to consider the allegations and their potential impact as a parent himself. “We understand families want answers quickly, but we must be thorough to identify every victim to protect the investigation and ensure families receive the right support,” Tsardoulias said. Police believe the images were taken between 2018 and 2023 at childcare centres at Rouse Hill and Putney, in Sydney’s north-west.
